_readme: Official OWCS calendar — EVENT-LEVEL source (Roadmap Phase B3).
This is the official-schedule adapter's data: competition dates, regional
stage windows, major-event dates and official broadcast destinations. It
is used to RECONCILE against FACEIT match facts (B4) — it never supplies
compositions and never silently overwrites FACEIT. When FACEIT and this
calendar disagree (e.g. start times), reconciliation raises a warning; a
human decides.
Entries here are a committed SEED/TEMPLATE for the 2026 season structure
(regional stages + global live events). Dates are placeholders marked
`verified: false` until confirmed against the official Overwatch Esports
schedule. `faceitCompetitionId` links an event to a registry competition
in config/faceit_competitions.json; a null link is exactly what B4 flags
as 'official event without a known FACEIT competition'.
No credentials, no scraping secrets — this file is committed so CI and
offline reconciliation run without network access.
VERIFICATION STATUS (2026-07-24): all events remain verified=false. The
official Overwatch Esports schedule site is NOT reachable from the
registry-config environment (network policy blocks non-registry hosts),
so no event date could be confirmed against an official source. Per the
task rule, verified stays false until an official source is available.
The FACEIT registry pass confirmed only the OWCS 2026 NA/EMEA Open
Qualifiers exist on FACEIT; the main-stage regional windows below are
unconfirmed placeholders.
UPDATE (2026-08-25): added `owwc_2026_group_stage`. The Overwatch
World Cup 2026 Group Stage (Days 1-4) aired on ow_esports_global
between 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-23 and no calendar event covered it, so
all four broadcasts sat unlinked. Its window is OBSERVED from the
broadcasts themselves rather than read from an official schedule (still
unreachable here), which is recorded per-entry in `dateProvenance` and
leaves verified=false. Nothing else aired in that window, so the link
is unambiguous on date alone — World Cup titles name no region, and
region is what normally separates same-window events.
